title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: vignette demonstrates create publication-quality Kaplan-Meier survival plots using survminer package visualization, gridify professional annotation layouts, tflmetaR centralized metadata management. workflow covers: Loading preparing ADTTE (Time--Event) data CDISC-compliant datasets Fitting survival models generating Kaplan-Meier curves Combining survival plots risk tables Annotating figures headers, titles, footnotes using gridify Integrating tflmetaR pull annotations external metadata files

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: begin loading necessary packages survival analysis, data manipulation, figure annotation.
code: library(tflmetaR) library(gridify) library(haven) library(dplyr) library(survival) library(survminer)

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: Analysis Dataset Time--Event (ADTTE) follows CDISC ADaM standards. use synthetic oncology dataset generated CDISC Dataset Generator, containing 3 treatment arms 500 subjects.
code: # get addtte data ---- # synthetic adtte for oncology therapeutic area from CDISC  adtte <- read_xpt(system.file("extdata", "adam_adtte.xpt", package = "tflmetaR"))

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: filter data Progression-Free Survival (PFS) analysis prepare survival modeling.
code: tte <- adtte |>   rename(avalc = AVALU) |>   rename_with(tolower) |>   filter(paramcd == "PFS") |>   arrange(desc(trtp)) |>   relocate(usubjid, trtp, cnsr, evntdesc, avalc, aval, trta) |>   select(usubjid, trtp, cnsr, evntdesc, avalc, aval, trta)  tte$trtp <- factor(tte$trtp)

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: create survival object fit Kaplan-Meier model stratified treatment group (trtp).
code: # run survival modal ---- surv_object <- Surv(time = tte$aval, event = tte$cnsr) fit1 <- survfit(surv_object ~ trtp, data = tte)

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: survminer package provides ggsurvplot() creating publication-ready Kaplan-Meier curves integrated risk tables, p-values, median survival lines.
code: # survial plot and table ---- ggsurv <- ggsurvplot(fit1,   data = tte, risk.table = TRUE, size = 1, # line size   pval = TRUE,   pval.size = 4,   pval.method = TRUE,   pval.method.size = 3,   fontsize = 3,   surv.median.line = "hv",   tables.theme = theme_survminer() +     theme(       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30"),       axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30"),       plot.title = element_text(size = 9),       element_text(size = 9, color = "red")     ) )

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: modify risk table labels display treatment group names readable format.
code: # risk table ----- t <- ggsurv$table +   scale_y_discrete(label = c("Treatment 3", "Treatment 2", "Treatment 1"))  p1 <- ggsurvplot(fit1, data = tte, risk.table = TRUE) ## can not add to the gridify directly

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: Using ggpubr::ggarrange(), combine survival plot risk table single figure proper alignment proportions.
code: # ggrance the survival plot  and risk table ---- p1 <- ggarrange(   ggsurv$plot + labs(x = "", y = "Survival Probability") +     scale_color_discrete() +     theme(       axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = 0, size = 9),       axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = -3, size = 9), # y axis label       axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30"), # tick values       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30"),       legend.title = element_blank()     ),   t + labs(y = "") +     theme(       axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = 0, size = 9),       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30")     ),   heights = c(2, 1.0),   ncol = 1, nrow = 2, align = "v" )

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: gridify package provides framework adding professional annotations figures, including headers, titles, footnotes, page numbers. pharma_layout_base() function creates layout compliant pharmaceutical industry standards.

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: example demonstrates manual annotation using gridify::set_cell() populate annotation field.
code: ## --- use gridify to annotate the figure --- fig <- gridify(   p1,   layout = pharma_layout_base(     margin = grid::unit(c(1, 1, 1.23, 1), "inches"),     global_gpar = grid::gpar(fontfamily = "Courier")   ) ) |>   set_cell("header_left_1", "UCB") |>   set_cell("header_left_2", "Drug X / Unspecified") |>   set_cell("header_left_3", "STUDY001") |>   set_cell("header_right_1", "CONFIDENTIAL") |>   set_cell("header_right_2", "Final") |>   set_cell("header_right_3", paste0("Data Cut-Off Date")) |>   set_cell("output_num", "Figure F01") |>   set_cell("title_1", "The Kaplan-Meier Curves of Progression-Free Survival Among Treatment Groups") |>   set_cell("title_2", "Population: Safety Set") |>   set_cell("title_3", "") |>   set_cell(     "note",     paste0(       "The synthetic oncology ADTTE was generated by CDISC Dataset Generator, ",       "with 3 treatment arms and 500 subjects.\n",       "Note: The Kaplan-Meier estimate of survival probability at a given time ",       "is the product of these conditional probabilities up until that given time."     ),     mchar = 132   ) |>   set_cell("footer_left", "Program: f_surv_gridify.R, Source(s): ADTTE") |>   set_cell("footer_right", paste0("Page ", 1, " of ", 1)) print(fig)

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: tflmetaR package enables separation metadata code storing titles, footnotes, headers external spreadsheets. approach: Centralizes annotations single location support audit traceability Reduces code complexity maintenance burden Supports regulatory compliance workflows

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: read titles header information Excel spreadsheet.
code: ## --- tflmetaR related code ----  # read headers, titles, and footnotes excel spreadsheet  file_name <- system.file("extdata", "st_titles.xls", package = "tflmetaR") title_file <- tflmetaR::read_tfile(filename = file_name, sheetname = "Sheet1") header_file <- tflmetaR::read_tfile(filename = file_name, sheetname = "Headr", validate = FALSE)  fig_number <- "Figure F01"

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: Using tflmetaR accessor functions, retrieve titles, footnotes, header content specific figure.
code: ulheader <- tflmetaR::get_ulheader(header_file)[1, ] urheader <- tflmetaR::get_urheader(header_file)[1, ] titles <- tflmetaR::get_title(title_file, tnumber = fig_number) footnotes <- tflmetaR::get_footnote(title_file, tnumber = fig_number, add_footr_tstamp = FALSE) pgmname <- tflmetaR::get_pgmname(title_file, tnumber = fig_number) source <- tflmetaR::get_source(title_file, tnumber = fig_number)  # convert footnote list to string footnote_str <- paste(unlist(footnotes), collapse = "\n")

title: Creating Kaplan-Meier Survival Plots with tflmetaR and gridify
text: Now combine gridify tflmetaR-extracted metadata create final publication-ready figure. approach ensures updates titles footnotes metadata spreadsheet automatically reflected output. can now preview annotated figure export result PDF file using gridify::export_to(fig2, "f_surv_tflmetar.pdf").
code: ## --- re-draw graph with pulled titles and footnotes ---- fig2 <- gridify(   p1,   layout = pharma_layout_base(     margin = grid::unit(c(0.5, 1, 0.25, 1), "inches"),     global_gpar = grid::gpar(fontfamily = "Courier")   ) ) |>   set_cell("header_left_1", ulheader[[1]]) |>   set_cell("header_left_2", ulheader[[2]]) |>   set_cell("header_left_3", ulheader[[3]]) |>   set_cell("header_right_1", urheader[[1]]) |>   set_cell("header_right_2", urheader[[2]]) |>   set_cell("header_right_3", urheader[[3]]) |>   set_cell("output_num", titles[[1]]) |>   set_cell("title_1", "") |>   set_cell("title_2", titles[[2]]) |>   set_cell("title_3", titles[[3]]) |>   set_cell("note", footnote_str, mch = 120) |>   set_cell("footer_left", paste0(     "Program: ", pgmname, ",  ",     "Source(s): ", source   )) |>   set_cell("footer_right", sprintf("Page %d of %d", 1, 1)) print(fig2)

title: Using tflmetaR with gt for Professional Tables
text: clinical research regulatory reporting, maintaining consistency accuracy table annotations—including titles, subtitles, footnotes, data sources—critical. Traditional approaches often embed annotations directly within analysis scripts, leading maintenance challenges, inconsistencies across outputs, increased risk errors updates. tflmetaR package addresses challenges implementing separation metadata code design pattern. externalizing table annotations structured spreadsheets (Excel CSV), tflmetaR enables: Centralized metadata management: titles, footnotes, source information stored single location support audit traceability Reduced code complexity: Analysis scripts remain focused data processing visualization Code stability: Metadata changes require modifications validated code Regulatory compliance: Supports audit-friendly workflows common pharmaceutical clinical settings vignette demonstrates integrate tflmetaR gt package create publication-quality tables externally managed annotations.

title: Using tflmetaR with gt for Professional Tables
code: library(tflmetaR) library(gt) library(dplyr)

title: Using tflmetaR with gt for Professional Tables
text: first step using tflmetaR loading metadata file contains table annotations. package supports Excel (.xlsx, .xls) CSV (.csv) formats read_tfile() function, optional sheet name Excel files. metadata file contain standardized columns including PGMNAME (program name), TTL1 (primary title), FOOT1 (first footnote), SOURCE (data source). Additional columns subtitles (TTL2, TTL3, …), additional footnotes (FOOT2, FOOT3, …), population definitions, bylines also supported. metadata file serves centralized repository table annotations, enabling consistent application across multiple outputs facilitating updates without code modifications.
code: # Load the sample metadata file included with the package file_path <- system.file("extdata", "sample_titles.xlsx", package = "tflmetaR")  # Read the metadata from the 'footer' sheet meta <- tflmetaR::read_tfile(filename = file_path, sheetname = "footer")  # Preview the structure of the metadata cat("Metadata columns:", paste(names(meta), collapse = ", ")) #> Metadata columns: TYPE, PGMNAME, OID, SOURCE, POPULATION, TTL1, TTL2, TTL3, BYLINE1, BYLINE2, BOOKM, FOOT1, FOOT2, FOOT3, FOOT4, FOOT5, FOOT6, FOOT7, FOOT8

title: Using tflmetaR with gt for Professional Tables
text: metadata loaded, tflmetaR provides suite accessor functions retrieve specific annotation components given table. Tables can identified TFL number (tnumber) program name (pname).

title: Using tflmetaR with gt for Professional Tables
text: function returns data frame non-missing fields, allowing flexible integration various table rendering packages.
code:
# Extract metadata components for a specific table # Tables are identified by their TFL number (e.g., "Table 2.1") tfl_number <- "Table 2.1"  title_info <- tflmetaR::get_title(meta, tnumber = tfl_number) footnotes <- tflmetaR::get_footnote(meta, tnumber = tfl_number, add_footr_tstamp = FALSE) source_info <- tflmetaR::get_source(meta, tnumber = tfl_number) population <- tflmetaR::get_pop(meta, tnumber = tfl_number) pgm_name <- tflmetaR::get_pgmname(meta, tnumber = tfl_number)  # Display extracted metadata cat("Title:", unlist(title_info$TTL1), "
") #> Title: Table 2.1 cat("Population:", unlist(population), "
") #> Population: Penguin Population cat("Program:", unlist(pgm_name), "
") #> Program: t_dm

title: Using tflmetaR with gt for Professional Tables
text: following example demonstrates create table title, subtitle, footnotes, source notes using metadata extracted via tflmetaR: gt package offers extensive customization options table styling, including: tab_header(): Adds title optional subtitle tab_footnote(): Adds footnotes precise location targeting tab_source_note(): Adds source attribution table footer tab_options(): Controls global table styling options
code:
# Prepare sample data sample_data <- mtcars |> head(5) |> select(mpg, cyl, hp, wt) |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ round(.x, 1))) # Extract annotation text from metadata using [[1]] notation main_title <- title_info$TTL1[[1]] subtitle <- title_info$TTL2[[1]] pop_text <- population$POPULATION[[1]] # Extract multiple footnotes foot1 <- footnotes$FOOT1[[1]] foot2 <- footnotes$FOOT2[[1]] source_text <- source_info$SOURCE[[1]] # Create the annotated gt table sample_data |> gt::gt() |> gt::tab_header( title = main_title, subtitle = gt::html(paste0(subtitle, "
", pop_text)) ) |> gt::tab_footnote( footnote = foot1, locations = gt::cells_column_labels(columns = mpg) ) |> gt::tab_footnote( footnote = foot2, locations = gt::cells_column_labels(columns = cyl) ) |> gt::tab_source_note( source_note = paste("Source:", source_text) ) |> gt::cols_label( mpg = "Miles/Gallon", cyl = "Cylinders", hp = "Horsepower", wt = "Weight (1000 lbs)" ) |> gt::tab_options( table.width = gt::pct(100), table.font.size = gt::px(14), heading.title.font.size = gt::px(16), heading.subtitle.font.size = gt::px(14) )

title: Manage Annotation Metadata in Statistical Outputs
text: tflmetaR provides simple interface retrieving titles, headers, footnotes tables, listings, figures (TFLs) clinical study reports (CSRs) formal deliverables metadata file. Best practices programming recommend separating code metadata improve readability, maintainability, scalability. However, many R scripts used clinical reporting still hardcode TFL annotations directly programs, making codebases difficult manage extend. tflmetaR bridges gap. Although independent self-contained, compatible {gridify} integrates Pharmaverse ecosystem generating submission-ready statistical deliverables. tflmetaR supports two workflows: concise single-function interface flexible helper-function workflow.

title: Manage Annotation Metadata in Statistical Outputs
text: can install newest release version CRAN:
code: install.packages("tflmetaR")

title: Manage Annotation Metadata in Statistical Outputs
text: metadata file can Excel file (.xlsx, .xls) CSV file (.csv), standardized column names. Required columns PGMNAME (program name), TTL1 (primary title), FOOT1 (first footnote), SOURCE (data source). Additional columns subtitles (TTL2, TTL3, …), footnotes (FOOT2, FOOT3, …), population definitions, book mark bylines also supported. file uses different column names, use change_colname() remap expected names passing file tflmetaR function.

title: Manage Annotation Metadata in Statistical Outputs
text: typical workflow retrieve annotation metadata metadata file apply TFL object created packages {gt}, {flextable}, {ggplot2}, lower-level grid tools grob gtable. Metadata can retrieved two ways. Option 1: Single-function interface Use tflmetaR() retrieve required metadata single call: Option 2: Helper-function workflow (recommended) Read metadata file read_tfile(), retrieve required metadata get_*() helper functions. avoids repeated /O operations annotating multiple fields:
code: path    <- system.file("extdata", "sample_titles.xlsx", package = "tflmetaR") pgmname <- "t_dm"  title_info <- tflmetaR(   path,   by_value         = pgmname,   annotation       = "TITLE",   add_footr_tstamp = FALSE )  footnotes  <- tflmetaR(   path,   by_value         = pgmname,   annotation       = "FOOTR",   add_footr_tstamp = FALSE ) meta       <- read_tfile(filename = path) title_info <- get_title(meta, pname = pgmname) footnotes  <- get_footnote(meta, pname = pgmname, add_footr_tstamp = FALSE)

title: Manage Annotation Metadata in Statistical Outputs
text: following example creates table using gt annotates titles footnotes retrieved metadata file using {tflmetaR}.  Note: Get image using gt::gtsave(tbl, "tbl.png")
code: library(tflmetaR) library(gt)  # Locate example metadata file path <- system.file("extdata", "sample_titles.xlsx", package = "tflmetaR") pgmname <- "t_dm"  # Retrieve annotation metadata (Option 2: helper-function workflow) meta <- read_tfile(filename = path) titles <- get_title(meta, pname = pgmname) footnotes <- get_footnote(meta, pname = pgmname, add_footr_tstamp = FALSE)  # Create the annotated gt table tbl <- mtcars |>   head(5) |>   gt::gt() |>   gt::tab_header(     title    = titles$TTL1[[1]],     subtitle = gt::html(titles$TTL2[[1]])   ) |>   gt::tab_footnote(footnote = footnotes$FOOT1[[1]]) |>   gt::tab_footnote(footnote = footnotes$FOOT2[[1]]) |>   gt::tab_options(table.width = gt::pct(80))

code: change_colname(input_xlsx, output_xlsx, config_path, sheet = NULL)

title: Standardize column names in the metadata file — change_colname
text: input_xlsx Path input Excel file. output_xlsx Path output Excel file create. config_path Path JSON configuration file containing column name mapping. sheet Sheet index name passed readxl::read_excel. NULL (default), first worksheet Excel file used.

title: Standardize column names in the metadata file — change_colname
text: Invisibly returns path output Excel file.

title: Standardize column names in the metadata file — change_colname
text: JSON configuration file must contain aliases field, named list mapping canonical field name character vector acceptable input column name variants. example:   matching, input column names aliases normalized converting lowercase, trimming whitespace, replacing underscores spaces. Columns match alias preserved unchanged. multiple input columns map canonical field name, output names made unique via base::make.unique().
code: {   "aliases": {     "TTL1": ["Title 1", "Title_1"],     "PGMNAME": ["Program Name", "program_name"]   } }

title: Standardize column names in the metadata file — change_colname
code: input_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx") output_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx") config_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")  example_df <- data.frame(   "Title_1" = "Summary of demographics",   "Program Name" = "t_dm",   check.names = FALSE )  writexl::write_xlsx(example_df, input_file)  cfg <- paste0(   "{",   '  "aliases": {',   '    "TTL1": ["Title 1"],',   '    "PGMNAME": ["Program Name"]',   "  }",   "}" )  writeLines(cfg, config_file)  change_colname(   input_xlsx = input_file,   output_xlsx = output_file,   config_path = config_file )  readxl::read_excel(output_file) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   TTL1                    PGMNAME #>   <chr>                   <chr>   #> 1 Summary of demographics t_dm

title: Single-call interface for retrieving annotation metadata — tflmetaR
text: Reads annotation metadata Excel (.xls, .xlsx) CSV (.csv) file returns requested metadata based annotation.

title: Single-call interface for retrieving annotation metadata — tflmetaR
code: tflmetaR(   filename,   sheetname = NULL,   by_column = "PGMNAME",   by_value,   oid = NULL,   annotation = NULL,   add_footr_tstamp = TRUE )

title: Single-call interface for retrieving annotation metadata — tflmetaR
text: filename Path metadata file. Supported formats .xls, .xlsx, .csv. sheetname Excel files, worksheet name index read. Ignored CSV files. NULL (default), first worksheet used. by_column Name column used identify desired row. Matching case-insensitive. Defaults "PGMNAME" (program name). by_value Value by_column used identify desired row. example, by_column = "PGMNAME" by_value = "t_dm.R" retrieves row PGMNAME == "t_dm.R". oid Optional object identifier additional row filtering. annotation Type annotation metadata return: NULL (default): return full filtered row. "TITLE": return title-related metadata (fields beginning "TTL", TTL1, TTL2, POPULATION available). "FOOTR": return footnote metadata (fields beginning "FOOT"). add_footr_tstamp = TRUE, timestamp line may appended. "SOURCE": return metadata fields beginning "SOURCE". "BYLINE": return metadata fields beginning "BYLINE". "POPULATION": return POPULATION field. string: return matching field(s) name. add_footr_tstamp Logical. TRUE (default), appends timestamp line footnote output annotation = "FOOTR".

title: Single-call interface for retrieving annotation metadata — tflmetaR
text: data frame containing selected metadata.

title: Single-call interface for retrieving annotation metadata — tflmetaR
text: tflmetaR() provides concise single-call interface retrieving annotation metadata. metadata file filtered single row matching by_value by_column (default: "PGMNAME"). multiple rows share by_column value, oid can used additional filtering. returned metadata reduced columns specified annotation. scripts annotate multiple fields, helper-function workflow recommended avoid repeated file /O: read metadata file read_tfile(), retrieve individual annotations get_title(), get_footnote(), related helpers.

title: Single-call interface for retrieving annotation metadata — tflmetaR
code: # Create a small example metadata file csv_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") write.csv(   data.frame(     PGMNAME = "t_dm",     TTL1 = "Table 14.1.1",     TTL2 = "Subject Disposition",     FOOT1 = "All Randomized Subjects",     SOURCE = "ADSL"   ),   csv_file,   row.names = FALSE )  # Return title-related columns tflmetaR(   filename = csv_file,   by_value = "t_dm",   annotation = "TITLE" ) #>           TTL1                TTL2 #> 1 Table 14.1.1 Subject Disposition  # Return footnote-related columns tflmetaR(   filename = csv_file,   by_value = "t_dm",   annotation = "FOOTR",   add_footr_tstamp = FALSE ) #>                     FOOT1 #> 1 All Randomized Subjects  # Return a specific column tflmetaR(   filename = csv_file,   by_value = "t_dm",   annotation = "SOURCE" ) #>   SOURCE #> 1   ADSL  # Return the full selected row tflmetaR(   filename = csv_file,   by_value = "t_dm" ) #>   PGMNAME         TTL1                TTL2                   FOOT1 SOURCE #> 1    t_dm Table 14.1.1 Subject Disposition All Randomized Subjects   ADSL
